arxiv-1805-03696.title: Bayeslands: A Bayesian inference approach for parameter uncertainty quantification in Badlands Journal: Computers & Geoscience
arxiv-1805-03696.creator: Rohitash Chandra, Danial Azam, R. Dietmar Müller, Tristan Salles, Sally Cripps
arxiv-1805-03696.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Rohitash Chandra, Danial Azam, R. Dietmar Müller, Tristan Salles, Sally Cripps. Bayesian inference provides a rigorous methodology for estimation and uncertainty quantification of parameters in geophysical forward models. Badlands (basin and landscape dynamics model) is a landscape evolution model that simulates topography development at various space and time scales. Badlands consists of a number of geophysical parameters that needs estimation with appropriate uncertainty quantification; given the observed present-day ground truth such as surface topography and the stratigraphy of sediment deposition through time.

arxiv-1908-08587.title: The Dirichlet problem for elliptic operators having a BMO anti-symmetric part Thanks: S. Hofmann acknowledges support of the National Science Foundation (grant number DMS-1664047, DMS-2000048). S. Mayboroda is supported in part by the NSF RAISE-TAQS grant DMS-1839077 and the Simons foundation grant
arxiv-1908-08587.creator: Steve Hofmann, Linhan Li, Svitlana Mayboroda, Jill Pipher
arxiv-1908-08587.description: Abstract . The present paper establishes the first result on the absolute continuity of elliptic measure with respect to the Lebesgue measure for a divergence form elliptic operator with non-smooth coefficients that have a BMO \BMO anti-symmetric part. In particular, the coefficients are not necessarily bounded.

arxiv-2211-04370.title: NESTER: An Adaptive Neurosymbolic Method for Causal Effect Estimation
arxiv-2211-04370.creator: Abbavaram Gowtham Reddy, Vineeth N Balasubramanian
arxiv-2211-04370.description: Abstract Causal effect estimation from observational data is a central problem in causal inference. Methods based on potential outcomes framework solve this problem by exploiting inductive biases and heuristics from causal inference. Each of these methods addresses a specific aspect of causal effect estimation, such as controlling propensity score, enforcing randomization, etc., by designing neural network (NN) architectures and regularizers.

arxiv-2304-02894.title: Affect as a proxy for literary mood
arxiv-2304-02894.creator: Emily Öhman, Riikka Rossi
arxiv-2304-02894.description: Abstract We propose to use affect as a proxy for mood in literary texts. In this study, we explore the differences in computationally detecting tone versus detecting mood. Methodologically we utilize affective word embeddings to look at the affective distribution in different text segments.

arxiv-2311-02359.title: Deformation of the Weighted Scalar Curvature
arxiv-2311-02359.creator: Pak Tung HO a and Jinwoo SHIN b
arxiv-2311-02359.description: Abstract Inspired by the work of Fischer–Marsden [ Duke Math. J. 42 (1975), 519–547], we study in this paper the deformation of the weighted scalar curvature. By studying the kernel of the formal L ϕ 2 L_{\phi}^{2} -adjoint for the linearization of the weighted scalar curvature, we prove several geometric results.

arxiv-2311-07033.title: TTMFN: Two-stream Transformer-based Multimodal Fusion Network for Survival Prediction Journal: Knowledge-Based Systems
arxiv-2311-07033.creator: Ruiquan Ge, Xiangyang Hu, Rungen Huang, Gangyong Jia, Yaqi Wang, Renshu Gu, Changmiao Wang, Elazab Ahmed, Linyan Wang, Juan Ye, Ye Li
arxiv-2311-07033.description: Abstract Survival prediction plays a crucial role in assisting clinicians with the development of cancer treatment protocols. Recent evidence shows that multimodal data can help in the diagnosis of cancer disease and improve survival prediction. Currently, deep learning-based approaches have experienced increasing success in survival prediction by integrating pathological images and gene expression data.

arxiv-2503-23735.title: Altermagnetism and Weak Ferromagnetism
arxiv-2503-23735.creator: I. V. Solovyev, S. A. Nikolaev, A. Tanaka
arxiv-2503-23735.description: Abstract Using a realistic model relevant to La 2 CuO 4 and other altermagnetic perovskite oxides, we study interrelations between weak ferromagnetism (WF), anomalous Hall effect (AHE), and net orbital magnetization (OM). All of them can be linked to the form of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions.

arxiv-2510-12685.title: Orderbook Feature Learning and Asymmetric Generalization in Intraday Electricity Markets
arxiv-2510-12685.creator: Runyao Yu 1 2 , Ruochen Wu 1 , Yongsheng Han 1 , Jochen L. Cremer 1 2
arxiv-2510-12685.description: Abstract Accurate probabilistic forecasting of intraday electricity prices is critical for market participants to inform trading decisions. Existing studies rely on specific domain features, such as Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) and the last price. However, the rich information in the orderbook remains underexplored.

arxiv-2511-20098.title: Studies of CPT symmetry in positronium decays with 192 plastic strip J-PET detector
arxiv-2511-20098.creator: N. Chug 1,2, S. D. Bass 1,3, E. Y. Beyene 1,2, C. Curceanu 4, E. Czerwiński 1,2, M. Das 1,2, K. V. Eliyan 1,2, M. Gorgol 5, J. Hajduga 6, S. Jalali 1,2, B. Jasińska 5, K. Kacprzak 1,2, T. Kaplanoglu 1,2, Ł. Kapłon 1,2, K. Kasperska 1,2, A. Khreptak 1,2, A. Kierys 7, G. Korcyl 1,2, T. Kozik 1,2, K. K
arxiv-2511-20098.description: Abstract A direct test of the CPT symmetry is performed for the electromagnetic decays of ortho-positronium using the J-PET tomograph. We present the precise measurement of the CPT-sensitive angular correlation entailing the positronium spin and the momenta of its annihilation photons, surpassing previous studies utilizing the same detection system.

pmc-10700836.title: Adaptation cannot keep pace with projected temperature increase
pmc-10700836.creator: Shuai Chen, Jie-Sheng Tan-Soo, Hai-Jian Ye
pmc-10700836.description: SummaryAn emerging argument is that since humans can readily adapt to changing climatic conditions, there is less need to pursue aggressive emissions mitigation strategies. As temperature adaptation is a function of repeated exposure over time, we need empirical approaches that can depict individuals’ temperature history to rigorously examine this claim.

pmc-11128730.title: Evaluation of Perinatal Outcomes in Pregnant Women With Low Amniotic Fluid Index
pmc-11128730.creator: Forozan Milani, Leila Khosousi, Seyedeh Hajar Sharami, Maryam Shakiba, Javid Rasoulian, Seyedeh Maryam Attari, Yalda Donyaei-Mobarrez
pmc-11128730.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective:The outcomes and management of low amniotic fluid index (AFI) in pregnancy are controversial. The purpose of this study was to determine the relationship between low AFI and perinatal outcomes.Materials and methods:This prospective study was conducted on 420 uncomplicated singleton pregnant women with a gestational age of over 28 weeks who referred to Al-Zahra Hospital in Rasht (Iran) for routine perinatal care. Pregnant women were divided into 3 groups of 140 patients based on the AFI and were followed up until delivery.

pmc-11420795.title: Safety and Immunogenicity of a Messenger RNA–Based Cytomegalovirus Vaccine in Healthy Adults: Results From a Phase 1 Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-11420795.creator: Carlos Fierro, Daniel Brune, Marian Shaw, Howard Schwartz, Conor Knightly, Jiang Lin, Andrea Carfi, Andrew Natenshon, Shiva Kalidindi, Caroline Reuter, Jacqueline Miller, Lori Panther
pmc-11420795.description: BackgroundThis phase 1 trial evaluated the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of mRNA-1647, a messenger RNA (mRNA)–based cytomegalovirus (CMV) vaccine, in CMV-seronegative and -seropositive adults.MethodsParticipants were randomly assigned to receive 30, 90, 180, or 300 µg of mRNA-1647 or placebo on a 0-, 2-, and 6-month schedule and followed for 12 months after the last dose.

pmc-11482706.title: Maternal total sleep deprivation causes oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in oocytes associated with fertility decline in mice
pmc-11482706.creator: Zi-Yun Yi, Qiu-Xia Liang, Qian Zhou, Lin Yang, Qing-Ren Meng, Jian Li, Yi-hua Lin, Yan-pei Cao, Chun-Hui Zhang, Heide Schatten, Jie Qiao, Qing-Yuan Sun
pmc-11482706.description: Previous studies have shown sleep deprivation is increasingly reported as one of the causes of female infertility. However, how and by what relevant mechanisms it affects female fertility remains unclear. In this study, female mice underwent 72 hours of total sleep deprivation (TSD) caused by rotating wheel or 2 different controls: a stationary wheel, or forced movement at night.

pmc-11650394.title: Cannabidiol for Scan-Related Anxiety in Women With Advanced Breast Cancer
pmc-11650394.creator: Manan M. Nayak, Peter Chai, Paul J. Catalano, William F. Pirl, James A. Tulsky, Stephanie C. Tung, Nancy U. Lin, Nicole Andrade, Sabrina Johns, Clint Vaz, Melissa Hughes, Ilana M. Braun
pmc-11650394.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Key PointsQuestionDoes cannabidiol (CBD) improve cancer-related anxiety?FindingsIn this phase II, double-masked, randomized clinical trial in 50 women with advanced breast cancer and clinical anxiety receiving CBD or placebo before a scan to assess tumor burden, a between-arm comparison of anxiety change before and after study drug ingestion was negative, even as anxiety levels after ingestion were significantly lower in the CBD vs placebo arm.

pmc-12384122.title: Antitumor Effects of Combination Therapy with Oncolytic Vaccinia Virus and Tepotinib on Lung Cancer Cells
pmc-12384122.creator: Takuya Inoue, Nobuhiro Kanaji, Takafumi Nakamura, Masanao Yokohira, Yuta Komori, Yasuhiro Ohara, Hitoshi Mizoguchi, Naoki Watanabe, Norimitsu Kadowaki, Akiteru Goto
pmc-12384122.description: Simple SummaryDespite recent advances in treatments for advanced lung cancer, survival rates remain low, emphasizing the need for new therapeutic strategies. This study evaluated the combined effects of an oncolytic vaccinia virus, engineered to selectively replicate in cancer cells, and the MET inhibitor tepotinib, known for its ability to enhance immune responses.

pmc-12606318.title: The serum platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio as a predictor of outcomes in bladder cancer patients: an updated meta-analysis
pmc-12606318.creator: Baining Zhang, Zhuoyue Yao, Zhongbao Zhou, Yong Zhang
pmc-12606318.description: There is conflicting evidence regarding the association between platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and the prediction of outcomes in bladder cancer (BCa). Due to the rapidly increasing availability of data to explore this issue, this updated meta-analysis investigates how pretreatment PLR influences the outcomes of BCa.

pmc-13281493.title: Pulmonary adverse events associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists: a systematic review of respiratory safety signals
pmc-13281493.creator: Aarushi Ahuja, Sai Prasad, Sahana Manoharan, Arya Sen, Richa Rana, Mansi Mody, FNU Paras, Archita Archita, Sana Shaik, Kartik Mehta, Rachel Manoj, Prakashini Mishra, Subhi Mehta, Pulkit Kapoor

pmc-13612721.title: First Contact Physiotherapists (FCPs) Referral Practices to Rheumatology: A Scoping Review of the Evidence Base
pmc-13612721.creator: Sarah Golding, Sue Innes, Anthony Smith, Jo Jackson
pmc-13612721.description: BackgroundFirst Contact Physiotherapists (FCP) are central to musculoskeletal practice within UK primary care, supporting patients at the earliest point of their healthcare journey. Early recognition and referral of rheumatological conditions are critical aspects of the role, necessitating knowledge, skills and capability.

pmc-13617432.title: Historical development of ADHD from 1753 to 2026
pmc-13617432.creator: Farzad Salehpour, Francisco Gonzalez-Lima
pmc-13617432.description: IntroductionThe conceptualization of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has evolved from early moral interpretations into a complex, multidimensional neurodevelopmental syndrome. This review traces the progressive convergence of clinical observation, developmental psychopathology, genetics, and behavioral neuroscience across history.MethodsWe synthesized historical literature, clinical milestones, neuroimaging data, and molecular genetics from the 18th century to the present.
